sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary hallway during morning drop-off

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Kevin, glad I caught you. I wanted to talk about the PTA agenda before next week's meeting.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Sure, what's up? I've got about ten minutes before I need to get to HGA. We have a design review at nine-thirty.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: How's the sustainable school design work going over there?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Busy. We just got a new commission for a charter school in Edina. But tell me about the PTA stuff.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: So as PTA president this year, I'm trying to push the health screening idea. Being a pediatrician, I see so many kids with undiagnosed vision issues, and I think we could catch a lot of that here at Burroughs.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: That's a great idea. Marcus was just saying the other day that he can't read the whiteboard from the back row. I should probably get his eyes checked.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Bring him into Children's Minnesota. I specialize in childhood asthma and allergies, but I can refer you to a great ophthalmologist in the building.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: I'll do that. How's Astrid liking fourth grade? Marcus says they're doing a big history project together.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: She loves it. She and Marcus make a good team. She's got her dad's history gene, I think.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Marcus told me Astrid knows more about the Civil War than their teacher. I believe it.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Ha! That's generous of him. Alright, I should get to the hospital. Let's sync on the fundraiser details this week?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Sounds good. I'll send you some ideas tonight.

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary school library during Wednesday volunteer shift

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: These new picture books came in. I love the illustrations in this one. The brushwork reminds me of Japanese woodblock prints.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: You would notice that. Does being a graphic designer ruin every book for you, or just the illustrated ones?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Every single one. I can't turn it off. I look at a book cover and immediately start thinking about kerning and color palette. It's a curse of freelancing from home — my brain never stops working.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: I get that. I'm the same way with app design. I'll be browsing something on my phone and start mentally filing UX bugs. Product manager brain doesn't shut off either.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That's right, you're at Target headquarters. How's the mobile app team?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Chaotic, as always. We're doing a big redesign of the checkout flow. But I'd rather talk about something fun. Lily and Sofia have been begging for a playdate this Saturday.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Those two are inseparable! It's adorable. They're in the same third-grade class, right?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Yeah, and apparently they've started a secret club. Lily won't tell me what it's about, but it involves a lot of whispering and giggling.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That's so sweet. Speaking of the girls, should we start the read-aloud for the first graders? I think they're lining up in the hallway.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Oh, it's that time already? I love this part of our Wednesday. Let me finish shelving these last few and I'll be right there.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I'll go get them settled. I picked a really good one today about a bear who learns to paint.

sessions.setting: Kevin's Tesla Model Y, Monday morning carpool to Burroughs Elementary

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Morning, Luis. Hop in. Marcus, scoot over so Diego has room back there.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Thanks for driving today. My Silverado's in the shop — something with the transmission. Had to have Maria drop me off.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: No problem. That's the beauty of our Monday-Wednesday-Friday carpool. We always have a backup.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I love this car, by the way. Still can't believe you charge it for free at the office.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: One of the perks of working at HGA. The charging station is right by my parking spot. So, hey, are you coming to the basketball game Saturday? I'm coaching the Burroughs team in the city rec league semifinals.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Semifinals! That's incredible. You really turned that team around this season.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: The kids have been working hard. Marcus is finally hitting his free throws consistently.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Sofia wants to try basketball next year. I told her she'd need to grow a few inches first.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Ha! Size isn't everything. Tell her to come by practice sometime. How's the restaurant doing?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: El Pueblito's been packed. Weekends are crazy. I barely get to sit down from Friday dinner service through Sunday brunch.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: That's a good problem to have. Maria must be a saint, holding things down at home on those nights.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: She really is. Alright, looks like we're here. Thanks for the ride, man.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Anytime. Have a good one.

sessions.setting: CorePower Yoga in Uptown, before their 6:30 AM class on a Friday

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: You beat me here today. I'm usually first to the 6:30 class.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Couldn't sleep. Erik was up grading papers until midnight and the light kept me awake. So I figured I'd get here early and stretch.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Well, at least we're consistent. Monday, Wednesday, Friday, every week. I think the instructor knows us by name at this point.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: She definitely does. She asked me last week if I was training for something because my flexibility has improved so much. I told her it's just stress relief from the hospital and PTA combined.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I get that. Oh, before I forget — Kai told me that Sofia Herrera and Lily Zhou are completely inseparable at school. Best friends in third grade. They do everything together. It's so sweet.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Astrid mentioned that too! Luis's daughter and Mei-Lin's daughter are like two peas in a pod. Anyway, have you thought more about teaching yoga? You mentioned it last time.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Actually, yes. I'm looking into the yoga teacher training at Yoga Sol. The 200-hour certification program. I want to be able to teach, not just practice. I'm nervous, though. It's a big time commitment.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: You should absolutely do it. Life's too short to put off the things that matter. Have you read 'Being Mortal' by Atul Gawande? It's my favorite book. It's really about living with purpose and not waiting.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I haven't, but I'll look it up. My go-to comfort read is 'The Tale of Genji.' A thousand-year-old novel about longing and beauty. Very different energy, but it also makes me think about how to spend my time.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: A thousand years old? That's incredible. Okay, class is about to start. Let's grab our spots.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Front row, as always. Let's do this.

sessions.setting: Upton Avenue South sidewalk, running into each other while checking mailboxes

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Hey neighbor! Haven't seen you all week. How's everything across the street?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Busy busy. I've been locked in my studio finishing illustrations for a rush project. A local bakery wants new branding by next week.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: You always make it look easy. Hey, I've been meaning to ask you — I saw a copy of 'Koi and the Moon' at the bookstore on Hennepin. Is that yours?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Yes! It just came out last month. The publisher is a small press here in Minneapolis. I'm so proud of it — it took me almost two years to finish the illustrations.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I bought a copy for Sofia. She loved it. The watercolors are beautiful.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That makes my day. Thank you, Luis. So what have you been up to? I've seen your truck loaded up with lumber a couple of times.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: That's for the school garden. I'm building three raised garden beds at Burroughs. I milled the cedar planks myself — got a buddy with a portable sawmill in Chaska.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: You're building them yourself? That's impressive.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: The garden program is really coming together. We're going to have the kids grow tomatoes, peppers, squash, herbs — the works. I want them to see where food comes from.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Kai would love that. He's been asking where vegetables grow. I think he thought they came from Target.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Ha! Well, tell him to come help me plant. The more little hands, the better. I'm hoping to get the beds in by the end of April before the ground warms up.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I will. And congratulations on the book thing — I mean, congratulations to me, but also thank you for buying it. It means a lot coming from a neighbor.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Of course. We Upton Avenue people stick together.

sessions.setting: Diane's backyard on Oliver Avenue, Friday evening while kids play

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: I love that we can just walk three doors down for a playdate. Oliver Avenue perks.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I know, it's the best. Lily and Astrid are already in the treehouse. Lars is trying to follow them up the ladder.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Your backyard looks amazing this year. Is that the vegetable garden you were talking about?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Yes! I went a little overboard. I've got tomatoes, cucumbers, zucchini, and a whole section of herbs. I'm hoping for a big tomato harvest this summer.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: My husband James would love fresh tomatoes. He's always complaining that the ones at the store taste like cardboard.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Tell James I'll bring some over when they're ready. How's his dental practice doing?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Busy. Spring is apparently when everyone remembers they haven't been to the dentist in a year. Hey, can I ask you something? You speak Swedish, right?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Conversational Swedish, yeah. My grandmother taught me growing up. She was the one who really pushed it — she didn't want the language to die in our family. Why do you ask?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Lily's been asking about learning other languages. She hears me speak Mandarin at home, and now she wants to know why everyone speaks something different. I was telling her about all the languages in our neighborhood.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: That's wonderful. This neighborhood really is a little United Nations. Hey, you mentioned you make xiaolongbao on Sundays. I've always wanted to learn. The folding technique looks impossible.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: It's actually not that hard once you get the wrist motion down. Come over this Sunday and I'll teach you. I make them from scratch every week — it's my meditation practice.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Deal. I'll bring some cardamom buns as a trade.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Ooh, yes please. Those are legendary.

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary, before the Japanese Cultural Day event

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Thank you both so much for helping me set up for Japanese cultural day. I can't do origami stations for eighty kids by myself.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Are you kidding? This is so fun. Lily was telling me about it all week. She loves anything crafty.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Diego's been practicing folding paper cranes at home. They look more like paper lumps, but the enthusiasm is there.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That's adorable. I also set up a calligraphy station. I'll be teaching them some basic Japanese characters. My Japanese gets a workout today.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: This reminds me — I need to start planning the Chinese New Year celebration for next February. The one this year was so much fun. We had a hundred and twenty students making dumplings.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I remember! Diego came home with dumpling filling all over his shirt and the biggest smile. He said it was the best day of school ever.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: That makes it all worth it. All three of us doing cultural events — it's like we're building a world tour at Burroughs.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I'm already planning the Cinco de Mayo fiesta for next month. I'm going to need both of you to help. We're talking piñata, folk dancing, a whole taco bar.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Count me in. We should coordinate calendars so the events don't overlap. The kids get so excited.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Diego's learning to read in both English and Spanish right now, so I want him to see that being bilingual is something to be proud of.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Absolutely. Lily's the same with Mandarin. It's so important for them to see their cultures celebrated at school.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Agreed. Okay, the kids are starting to come in. Let me get the origami paper organized. Station one, everyone!

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary parking lot after school, discussing the playground project

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Diane, come look at the playground site. The construction crew broke ground this morning.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Already? That's amazing! I drove the Volvo past it during drop-off and thought something was happening but didn't have time to stop.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Yeah, my XC90-driving PTA president — always in a rush.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Ha ha. So tell me about the design. You've been working on this for months.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: The whole thing is built from recycled materials. Reclaimed wood for the climbing structure, recycled rubber for the ground cover, even the metal is repurposed steel from a demolished warehouse in Northeast. Should be done by the end of summer.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: That's so on-brand for you. Sustainable everything. The kids are going to love it.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Speaking of kids, my after-school architecture club on Thursdays is doing a mini design challenge related to the playground. Twelve students building scale models of their dream play spaces.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: That's a brilliant way to get them involved. Astrid mentioned it, actually. She said Marcus was building a model with slides going in every direction.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: That sounds about right. He dreams big. Hey, are you bringing those cardamom buns to Tuesday's PTA meeting?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Of course. Kardemummabullar for every PTA meeting — it's tradition at this point. I'd start a revolt if I showed up empty-handed.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: You really would. Those things are addictive. Alright, I should head home. Dupont Avenue is calling.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Same. The Tuesday-Thursday carpool starts early tomorrow. See you at the meeting!

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary Cinco de Mayo fiesta preparation

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Alright, the taco bar is set up, the piñata is hung, and Los Hermanos del Norte should be here in an hour to do the music.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: This looks incredible, Luis. How many people are you expecting?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: About three hundred. I've been up since four prepping tortillas. I make them fresh every morning at El Pueblito anyway, but today I tripled the batch. Heirloom corn masa from that farm in Iowa — nothing else compares.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: The smell alone is worth the trip. I drove the BMW over early to help with setup. Lily's been talking about the piñata for two weeks straight.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Marcus and Zoe are both beyond excited. Being a single dad, these school events are a lifesaver. It's hard to create the big celebration feel at home when it's just the three of us.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Kevin, you do an amazing job with those kids. Marcus is one of the kindest boys in that school.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Thanks, Mei-Lin. That means a lot. Since the divorce in 2021 it's been... an adjustment. But Marcus and Zoe are my whole world.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: And you've got all of us. That's what this parent group is about. Hey, I need someone to drive my truck over to the restaurant to grab the last batch of elote. Kevin, you up for it?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Your red Silverado? Sure, I'll take it. Where are the keys?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: On the dashboard. Just be careful — the clutch sticks a little.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: I'll organize the folk dancing area while you're gone. I'm taking the kids to Mandarin class after this, so I need to wrap up by two.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Perfect. This is going to be the best Cinco de Mayo Burroughs has ever seen.

sessions.setting: Linden Hills Coffee, lunch break meeting to discuss yearbook design

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: So I have some news. I won the AIA Minnesota Honor Award for the Hmong Cultural Center design in St. Paul.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Kevin! That's huge! Congratulations! When did you find out?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Last night. I was reading my emails while Marcus was doing homework and almost fell out of my chair. You know that building took me two years. I really poured my heart into it.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: You deserve it. Cultural spaces matter so much. It reminds me of something Jane Jacobs wrote — communities need these gathering places.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: You've read Jane Jacobs? 'The Death and Life of Great American Cities' is my absolute favorite book. She understood cities better than any architect I know.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I read it when I was working on the Burroughs yearbook cover. I was thinking about what makes a school community feel alive, and someone recommended it. Speaking of which, the yearbook cover is done.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Can I see it?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Here, on my phone. I did watercolor portraits of all twenty-two teachers. Each one has a little detail that represents their subject or personality.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Tomoko, this is stunning. The kids are going to treasure this.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I hope so. Ryan says I spent too long on it, but he's a firefighter — he thinks anything that takes more than sixty seconds is overthinking.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Ha! How is Ryan? Station 28 keeping him busy?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Always. Lake Street never sleeps. He had a three-alarm call last week and came home smelling like smoke for two days. But he loves it.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Respect. Alright, I should head back. Got to drive the CX-5 or the Tesla today?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: The Mazda, as always. Still rocking my Minneapolis Parks bumper sticker. Wouldn't trade it for anything.

sessions.setting: Diane's kitchen on Oliver Avenue, Sunday xiaolongbao-making session

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Okay, fold the edge in, pinch and twist. Like this — see how it makes those little pleats?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I think I'm getting it... wait, that one burst open. Ugh.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: You're getting better! The first dozen are always sacrificial. My grandmother in Shanghai didn't let me make them for real until I'd practiced for a month.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Speaking of family trips — Erik and I are taking the kids to Stockholm in a few weeks. We're visiting my cousin Ingrid for Midsommar. It'll be Lars's first time in Sweden.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: That sounds magical. We're planning a trip to Shanghai in July. My grandmother is turning ninety, and I want Lily to be there for the celebration.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Ninety! That's incredible. Your dad must be excited too.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Oh, Dr. Wei Zhou is already planning the party. He's retired from the physics department at the University of Minnesota but somehow busier than ever.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Funny how retirement works. Hey, didn't you just run Grandma's Marathon?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Last weekend! The half-marathon in Duluth. Two hours and five minutes. I'm still sore, but I'm so proud I finished.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Two-oh-five is great! I'm thinking about signing up for the Twin Cities Marathon in October. The full marathon, though. Am I crazy?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: A little, but you're a pediatrician who does yoga three times a week and still has energy left over. If anyone can do it, it's you. How's Erik handling all your activities?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: He teaches AP U.S. History at Southwest High, so he's got his own chaos. We barely see each other during the school year. But summers are our time.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: James is the same. Linden Hills Family Dental keeps him running all day, and then he comes home and just wants to collapse on the couch. Alright, next batch. Try the pinch-twist again.

sessions.setting: Tomoko's home studio on Upton Avenue, Friday evening, working on El Pueblito menu redesign

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I still can't believe you designed the El Pueblito logo back in 2022. Every time someone compliments the branding, I think of you.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That was such a fun project. The chili pepper motif with the Puebla cathedral silhouette — I did a lot of research into the architecture of your hometown to get it right.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: It means a lot that you took the time. Puebla is so beautiful. I moved to Minneapolis when I was eighteen, and I still miss the colors of the zocalo every day.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I understand that feeling. I moved here from Kyoto in 2014 after I married Ryan. He was teaching English in Japan, and we met through mutual friends. Minneapolis is home now, but Kyoto is always in my heart.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: At least you married someone adventurous. Ryan went halfway around the world to teach English. That's bold.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: And then became a firefighter here. He does nothing halfway. Speaking of family, my mother Sachiko sent me a package last week. She's a kimono maker in Kyoto — has been for forty years. She sent fabric samples for a project I'm working on.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: A kimono maker? That's such a beautiful craft. My mother Rosa is the same way with mole sauce — she's been perfecting her recipe for decades. It's an art form.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I love that. What cookbook do you reach for when you need inspiration?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Bricia Lopez's 'Oaxaca: Home Cooking from the Heart of Mexico.' Every time I open it, I find something new. The mole negro recipe alone is worth the price.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I should get a copy. Maybe it'll inspire some food illustrations. Okay, let me show you the new menu layout. I changed the typeface and reorganized the sections.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Let's see it. You always make El Pueblito look better than it deserves.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Impossible. The food speaks for itself. I'm just making the wrapper pretty.

sessions.setting: Kevin's backyard on Dupont Avenue South, annual Fourth of July barbecue

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Welcome, everyone! Thirty-five guests and counting. I think this is our biggest Fourth of July yet.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Kevin, you've outdone yourself. The backyard looks amazing. Lars, stop trying to eat the sparklers, they're not candy!

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Don't worry, Los Hermanos del Norte is setting up in the corner. We'll have live mariachi music in about twenty minutes. I tuned up my guitar this morning just for this.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Live music! The kids are going to love it. Where did you set up the food, Kevin?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Buffet table by the grill. I was up at six making eggs benedict for Marcus and Zoe — that's our weekend tradition — and then started on the burgers. Weekdays they get pancakes, weekends they get the fancy stuff.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: You cook breakfast for them every single morning? Kevin, that's incredible.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Every morning. It's our time together before the day gets crazy.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: That's just beautiful. Oh, Kevin, is your mom here? I've been wanting to meet her.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: She's inside with the kids. Mom — Gloria — retired from being a school principal and now she tutors neighborhood kids at the St. Paul Public Library. She can't stop teaching.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: That's so sweet. Educators never really retire, do they?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: They don't. My mom Rosa is the same way with cooking — she's back in Puebla but still calls me every week to critique my salsa recipe.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Ha! Lars, come here for a second. Everyone, look how big this kid has gotten. He's in first grade now and already playing peewee soccer. He scored two goals last week.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Kai's on the same team as Lars! He talks about soccer constantly. It's his favorite thing after school.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Alright, burgers are ready! Come and get it, everyone. Happy Fourth!

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary school garden, Friday morning watering session

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Look at these tomato plants, Mei-Lin. They're going to produce like crazy this year. I'm estimating at least a hundred and twenty pounds across all three beds.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: That's incredible. And all of it goes to the school cafeteria?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Every pound. The kids eat what they grow. It's the whole point of the garden program.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: You know, this reminds me of community gardens in Shanghai. I was born there, and my neighborhood had these little plots between the apartment buildings. I moved here when I was fourteen — my dad got a research position at the University of Minnesota — and I missed those gardens for years.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: That's a big move at fourteen. Must have been tough.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: It was. But Minneapolis has been good to me. I actually built a Little Free Library in front of our house on Oliver Avenue last month. I stocked it with bilingual English-Mandarin children's books.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I saw that! Sofia and Lily were looking at the books together last week. Lily was translating the Mandarin for Sofia.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: That's the dream. I also teach a weekend Mandarin class at the Minnesota Chinese Cultural Center. Fifteen students, including Lily. I want these kids to be proud of their heritage.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I feel exactly the same way. That's why I started the Saturday kids' cooking class at El Pueblito. I teach it in Spanish. Did I tell you the Star Tribune gave us 'Best New Restaurant' back in 2022?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: You did, and you deserved it. El Pueblito is the real deal. Sofia drags Lily there at least once a month.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Those girls are inseparable. Alright, help me with the peppers? The jalapeños need more water than I thought.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: On it. Hand me that hose.

sessions.setting: Kevin's home office on Dupont Avenue, reviewing design club materials

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: I just got back from Copenhagen last week. Five days, six schools. Danish school architecture is light-years ahead of what we're doing here.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Six schools in five days? That's intense. What stood out?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: The way they integrate outdoor learning spaces. Every school had gardens, courtyards, natural materials. I took about five hundred photos. I'm going to use some of the ideas for my architecture club at Burroughs.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: The kids in your Thursday club must love getting real-world inspiration like that. Speaking of projects, did Marcus ever finish that LEGO model?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: The Foshay Tower? Yes! Thirty-two hundred pieces, and we built every single one together. It's on display at the school art fair right now.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That's amazing. I should take Kai to see it. He loves building things. Hey, unrelated — are you really learning Mandarin on Duolingo?

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Ha, yeah. Marcus's best friend speaks Mandarin at home, and I felt silly not knowing anything. So I started Duolingo about three months ago. I can order food and say 'Where is the bathroom?' Very useful skills.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That's so thoughtful. You're a good dad, Kevin.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: I try. How's your Saturday art class at the community center going?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: It's wonderful. I get ten to fifteen kids every week at the Linden Hills Community Center. Last Saturday we did watercolor landscapes of Lake Harriet. The talent in these kids is unreal.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: That's great. Does Kai go?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: He does, but mostly for the snacks. Oh, that reminds me — I need to prep his bento box for tomorrow. I make him one every school day with a different character theme using nori and vegetables. Tomorrow is a panda.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: You make character bento boxes every day? That is next-level parenting.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: It's my love language. And Kai's too picky to eat a normal lunch, so I have to make it fun.

sessions.setting: CorePower Yoga in Uptown, after Friday morning class

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That class was exactly what I needed. I just got back from Kyoto with Kai, and my body is still on Japan time.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: How was the trip? You went for the Gion Matsuri festival, right?

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: It was magical. Kai got to see the grand procession of floats, and my parents spoiled him rotten. Two weeks of my mom's home cooking and he doesn't want to eat anything I make anymore.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Ha! Kids are so loyal to grandma's cooking. How's Kai adjusting to being back? Second grade starts in a couple weeks.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: He's excited. He keeps asking about peewee soccer. He and Lars are on the same team, so he's been texting Lars — well, texting me to text you to text Lars — about practice schedules.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Lars is the same way. Soccer is all he talks about. By the way, I finished my yoga teacher training through you-know-where!

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Wait, I thought I was the one doing the teacher training! I finished the 200-hour certification at Yoga Sol in June!

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: No no, I mean I'm inspired BY your certification to think about it eventually. You did it — I'm just dreaming about it. I'm too busy. Between the hospital, PTA, and the free clinic, I barely have time to breathe.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: The free clinic? Tell me about that.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I volunteer at a free clinic in the Phillips neighborhood every other Saturday morning. Uninsured children, mostly. A lot of them have never seen a doctor. It's heartbreaking but important.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Diane, you're incredible. How do you do everything?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Coffee. Lots of coffee. And I signed up for the Twin Cities Marathon in October, so apparently I enjoy suffering. I've been training on the weekends when I'm not at the clinic.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: You are going to crush it. I'll be at the finish line cheering for you.

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary cafeteria, setting up for the Mid-Autumn Festival

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Two hundred mooncakes, all baked and boxed. My kitchen looks like a bakery exploded in it.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Two hundred? Mei-Lin, that's insane. When did you even have time?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: I baked all last weekend. James stayed out of the kitchen and just kept bringing me tea. He knows not to interfere when I'm in mooncake mode.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: They look beautiful. The lotus paste ones are my favorite. Should I set up the decoration table over here?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Yes, perfect. This reminds me of the Chinese New Year celebration I organized here in February. We had a hundred and twenty students making dumplings. The cafeteria was covered in flour for days.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I remember that! Lars came home with dumpling dough in his hair. He wanted to make them at home every night for a week. Speaking of the library, Mei-Lin — did you see the new books I put in?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: The ones with the dedication plaque? Yes! Lily checked out three of them last week.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I donated fifty children's books in memory of my mother. She was a librarian her whole career. Books were her whole world, and I wanted Burroughs to have a piece of that.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: That's so touching, Diane. Those books are going to mean so much to the kids.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: They already do. Hey, speaking of books — have either of you read 'Educated' by Tara Westover?

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I haven't, but I keep hearing about it.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: It's my favorite book. It's about education as liberation, basically. Growing up, moving to a new country at fourteen, education was my lifeline. This book captured that feeling perfectly.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I'll add it to my list. Okay, the parents are starting to arrive. I think we're ready for this Mid-Autumn Festival. Mei-Lin, this is going to be wonderful.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: I also set up the piano in the corner. I'm going to play a few traditional pieces during the celebration. I perform with the Linden Hills Community Orchestra, so I should be able to handle a solo. We do two concerts a year at the Lake Harriet Bandshell. Next one is in November — you're both invited.

sessions.setting: Burroughs Elementary auditorium, after the school-wide health screening event

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Three hundred and forty students screened. Vision and hearing for every kid in the school. I am exhausted but so happy we pulled this off.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: You organized the whole thing, Diane. The volunteer doctors, the equipment, the scheduling — that was all you.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: It takes a village. Literally. We caught twelve kids with undiagnosed vision problems and eight with hearing issues. That's twenty families who now know something they didn't before.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: That's incredible. Diego was a little scared of the hearing test, but the nurse was great with him. Hey, speaking of good news — I finalized the catering menu for the fall gala next month. Tacos al pastor, elote, and churros for two hundred guests.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Luis, you're a legend. That gala is going to be amazing. Diane and I have been working on the fundraising side for weeks.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Speaking of the gala — Kevin, is Zoe doing a performance? Someone mentioned the music.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: She is! She takes violin at MacPhail Center for Music every Saturday. She did the spring recital in May and now her teacher wants her to play at the gala. She's been practicing like crazy.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: That's wonderful. A little girl on violin with tacos al pastor in the background. Only at Burroughs.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Ha! My mom was actually at Zoe's recital. She drove over from St. Paul just to watch. She grew up in the Rondo neighborhood — still has that community spirit, always showing up for the kids.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Oh, and Luis — Lars's soccer team just finished the fall season. Undefeated! I coached them all season and I can barely believe it. I know nothing about soccer.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Undefeated! That's amazing, Coach Johansson.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Don't call me that. I literally just yelled 'Kick the ball!' every game. The kids did all the work.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Still counts. Alright, let's clean up and get out of here. It's been a long day.

sessions.setting: Kevin's living room on Dupont Avenue, post-marathon celebration for Diane

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: To Diane! Three hours and fifty-two minutes! Twin Cities Marathon finisher!

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: I can barely walk, but thank you all for being at the finish line. I saw your signs and almost started crying at mile twenty-four.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: You earned it. I couldn't even finish a full marathon — my half at Duluth nearly killed me. But three fifty-two is incredible.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: I brought champagne and tamales. Proper celebration fuel.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: And I brought mochi from the Japanese market. Sweet rice for the sweet champion.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: You guys are the best. This whole year has been so much. The PTA, the marathon, the health screening...

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: Speaking of PTA — our fall gala is next month and we need to talk numbers. As co-chairs of the fundraising committee, we should probably set a target.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: Right, let's be ambitious. I think we can hit eighteen thousand this year.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Oh, I have news too. I took Lily to Shanghai in July to visit my grandmother's ninetieth birthday. And while we were there, Lily's Mandarin improved so much. She's been on a roll since we got back. She just won the Burroughs spelling bee last week!

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: The spelling bee! What was the winning word?

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Chrysanthemum. Ironic, since the Chinese word for it is simpler.

turns.speaker: diane
turns.text: That's amazing, Mei-Lin. Lily is such a sharp kid. Oh, Kevin, I keep meaning to ask — did you know my parents still run a Swedish bakery on Superior Street in Duluth? I grew up there. Johansson's bakery. I should bring some of their pastries for the gala.

turns.speaker: kevin
turns.text: A Swedish bakery in Duluth? Yes, please bring everything they have.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Between Diane's Swedish pastries and my taco bar, this gala is going to be the best-catered event in Minneapolis history.

sessions.setting: El Pueblito restaurant, after hours, planning end-of-year school events

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Thanks for meeting here after closing. I made some guacamole and we've got the whole place to ourselves.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: I love El Pueblito after hours. It's so peaceful compared to the dinner rush.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: It's busy, but that's a blessing. And we've been giving back — El Pueblito donates thirty meals a week to the Burroughs free lunch program. Those kids deserve real food, not just packaged stuff.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Thirty meals a week! That's incredible, Luis. Does the school cover any of the cost?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: A little, but mostly it's on us. Maria says I'm going to bankrupt us, but she's a labor and delivery nurse at Abbott Northwestern — she understands feeding people in need.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: How's Diego adjusting to kindergarten?

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: He's great. We took the whole family to Puebla in April for my nephew's first communion. My mother Rosa cooked for three days straight. Diego ate so many tamales I thought he'd burst. Coming home and going back to school was a tough transition.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Family trips like that are everything. Hey, I have exciting news. I secured a twenty-five-thousand-dollar grant from Target's community fund for the new all-weather track at Burroughs. Pitched it to the giving committee and they approved it in one meeting.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Twenty-five thousand! Mei-Lin, that's huge!

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: First the playground from Kevin, now the track from you. Burroughs is getting a serious upgrade.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: And I have news too. 'Koi and the Moon' got nominated for a Minnesota Book Award. I just found out. The ceremony is in January. I'm nervous but so grateful.

turns.speaker: meilin
turns.text: Tomoko! A Book Award nomination! We'll all be there cheering for you.

turns.speaker: luis
turns.text: Just like we cheered for Diane at the marathon. This group shows up for each other. Five parents who met because our kids go to the same school, and now we're basically family.

turns.speaker: tomoko
turns.text: Basically family. I'll drink guacamole to that. Wait — you don't drink guacamole. You know what I mean.
